Answer: C
Reason: The CT images demonstrate extensive pneumomediastinum and subcutaneous emphysema extending into the neck (Figure 3), with air clearly visible within the spinal canal (pneumorrhachis). In the absence of direct trauma or esophageal perforation signs, the most accepted pathway for spontaneous pneumorrhachis in this context is air tracking from the mediastinum/retropharyngeal space through the cervical neural exit foramina into the epidural space.
